name: lot_developer_geometry_cost_rubble_count
description: Tests 10 and 11 (§11.4, §7.3, §16), shipped cost curve. GetAreaSlope walks the vertices x1..x2+1 (outer), z1..z2+1 (inner); the first strict minimum and maximum give lo/hi and their vertices; the distance between them is scaled in cascade (quirk 12): >6 x0.25, >5 x0.3, >4 x0.35 (then return), >3 x0.4. GetLotDevelopmentCost: s = slope x 0.0625, cost = trunc(curve(s) x w x h). Test 10, 1x1 lot (vertices (0,0)..(1,1)), altitude 100 except vertex (1,0) = 104: lo 100 at (0,0) [first], hi 104 at (1,0); dx 1, dz 0, d = 1.0, not > 3 so no scaling; slope = (104-100)/1 = 4.0; s = 0.25; curve(0.25) interpolates the (0,0)-(0.555556,10) segment -> 4.499996; cost = trunc(4.499996 x 1 x 1) = 4. A flat rectangle gives slope 0 (lo = hi, distance 0) -> cost 0. Test 11, rubble count: area = dz x dx, count = trunc(area x 2^-7) + 4; small = dx<10 or dz<10 (corners get nothing); large = dx>12 and dz>12 (corners draw a type). 11x11 -> area 121, count 4 (trunc(0.9453125) + 4), not small, not large; 8x8 -> small; 16x16 -> area 256, count 6 (two interior props), large.

steps.note: vertex index 1 = (x=1, z=0) since vertsX = 65; all others default 100
a larger flat rectangle with the same single peak still has lo 100 hi 104
test 10 row 2: a 2x3 lot (x 0-1, z 0-2), altitude 100 except vertex (2,3) = 260; index 2 + 3*65 = 197
s ~ 6.934 clamps the curve to 3000; cost trunc(3000 * w2 * h3) = 18000
12x12 -> area 144, count trunc(1.125)+4 = 5, not large (>12 strict)
10x20 -> area 200, count 5, neither side > 12 so not large
